newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SPAIN REIGN ON CLAY AS GERMANY GO DOWN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPAIN REIGN ON CLAY AS GERMANY GO DOWN.

text.p: Albert Costa and Felix Mantilla both posted straight-set wins as Spain sped to victory over Germany at the World Team Cup on Thursday.
Cold, rainy conditions twice delayed play three hours and forced the postponement of the doubles, but failed to cool off the red-hot Spaniards who have dominated on clay this season.
A Spaniard has filled 14 of the 28 semifinal spots in seven European clay court events this season, winning four.
That domination has been in evidence at the World Team Cup.
In two ties Spain have yet to lose a match and dropped just two sets, leaving them top of the Blue Group standings with a perfect 2-0.
Although Mantilla's match took most of the day to complete, after it was interupted midway through the first set, he spent little time on court crushing David Prinosil 6-2 6-1 in 41 minutes.
With rain continually threatening his match, Costa made quick work of Michael Stich, disposing of the 1991 Wimbledon champion 6-1 6-3 in exactly one hour.
"The long wait was difficult but you get used to it, you just have to try and be patient and keep your concentration," said Costa, world ranked 13th.
"Today was a very good match for me, I kept Micheal at the baseline and never let him in to the net."
Immediately after the match, Stich said he would not play at the French Open, joining a growing list of players to drop out of the Grand Slam event starting on Monday.
Stich, who lost in the final of last year's French Open to Yevgeny Kafelnikov, said a nagging shoulder injury had grown worse, to the point where his serve was almost completely ineffective.
"I'm serving at about 40 percent and when I try to serve harder the pain is worse," he said.
In the other Blue Group tie, Sweden and the Netherlands battled each other to a 1-1 draw.
Magnus Larsson gave the Swedes a 1-0 lead when he defeated Paul Haarhuis 2-6 6-3 6-2.
But Jan Siemerink levelled the tie with an upset 6-2 7-6 over world number nine Thomas Enqvist.
Due to darkness, the doubles rubber was rescheduled for Friday.
